{{Ship module infobox}}

The '''Detailed Surface Scanner''' ('''DSS''') is a Class 1 optional internal module that launches replenishing probes to map planets and moons or scan [[Planetary Rings|planetary rings]]. Planetary mapping increases exploration-data value, reveals applicable surface signals, and supports current Live [[Exobiology]]. Ring scans reveal [[Mining Hotspot|mining hotspots]].<ref name="frontier-beyond">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/en-US/news/elite-dangerous-beyond-chapter-four-out-now Elite Dangerous: Beyond – Chapter Four – Out Now], Frontier Developments, 11 December 2018. Accessed 10 September 2026.</ref>

The DSS follows system discovery and Full Spectrum System Scanner identification. It does not replace those integrated scanners or the ship's [[Sensors]].

Probes replenish automatically and do not consume cargo or require station restocking. The module operates only in Supercruise and Analysis Mode.

== Operating requirements ==

Surface Scanner must be assigned to a fire group. The ship must be in Supercruise, the intended body must be targeted and within range, and Analysis Mode must be active. Activating the fire-group control opens the DSS interface.

For the complete ordered workflow, see [[How to Map a Planet or Moon with a Detailed Surface Scanner]].

== Planetary mapping mechanics ==

Each probe maps a circular area around its point of impact. The size of that area is controlled by '''Probe Radius'''. Probes aimed directly at the disc cover the near side; probes aimed just beyond the limb follow curved trajectories to the far side. The interface provides front and back coverage views.

A planetary map completes when probe coverage reaches 90%. The scanner fills the remaining gaps and reports the body at 100%, so every last visible patch does not need a separate probe.<ref name="dss-community" />

=== Probe Efficiency Target ===

Each mappable body displays a Probe Efficiency Target. Completing the map with no more than that number of probes earns the efficiency bonus. Exceeding the target does not invalidate the map; it only forfeits that bonus.

Increasing Probe Radius covers more surface per impact and makes the target easier to meet.

=== Mapping results ===

A completed map provides more valuable exploration data than discovery alone and can reveal persistent points of interest or signal filters. If a previously unmapped body's data is submitted before another Commander's result, the system map can permanently show that Commander under '''First Mapped By'''. Mapping alone does not secure the tag; the data must be submitted.

== Signals Filter ==

On a mapped body with biological or geological activity, the DSS surface view provides a '''Signals Filter'''. A signal count is the number of detected signal types, not the number of individual specimens or formations.

In current Live Exobiology, each detected genus can be selected separately. The blue overlay shows terrain in which that genus can occur. It is not an organism-density heat map and does not identify an exact colony; darker-looking blue does not reliably mean more life.<ref name="frontier-overlay">[https://issues.frontierstore.net/issue-detail/31345 Issue 31345: Detailed Surface Scanner heat map], Frontier Issue Tracker. The acknowledged design response describes the display as areas where organics are likely to be found rather than a density heat map. Accessed 10 September 2026.</ref>

For the practical search workflow, see [[How to Choose an Exobiology Search Area with a Detailed Surface Scanner]].

=== Biological signals ===

{{#invoke:SurfaceSignals|table|type=Biological|links=no}}

{{Unverified claim|Older pre-Odyssey structures such as Amphora Plants, Anemones, Bark Mounds, Brain Trees, Crystalline Shards, and Sinuous Tubers are separate from Odyssey's genus system. Their exact presentation as individually named, general, or absent filters in the current Live DSS has not been confirmed.}}

'''Fumerola''' is an Exobiology genus. '''Fumarole''' is a geological vent. Their similar names do not make them aliases.

=== Geological signals ===

Geological filters follow the same broad rule: highlighted terrain is suitable for the selected feature, not an exact formation marker.

{{#invoke:SurfaceSignals|table|type=Geological|links=no}}

== Ring-scanning capability ==

A probe that intersects a ring scans that ring band and reveals any mining-hotspot regions. A hotspot narrows the search area for its named commodity but does not identify an individual valuable asteroid. The ring scan is separate from mapping the planet or moon it surrounds.

See [[How to Scan Planetary Rings for Mining Hotspots]] for the complete procedure, then continue with the method selected through [[Mining]].

== Engineering and variants ==

The standard DSS accepts '''Expanded Probe Scanning Radius''' Engineering. It increases Probe Radius and has no experimental effect. Engineer pages and [[Engineering Blueprints]] own the individual workshop grades, costs, and unlock requirements.
